FACTUAL POSITION & PLEADINGS 1.

Vide this judgment/award, this Tribunal shall decide claim of compensation on account of death of Master Inder Yadav in a road vehicular accident which took place on 18.05.2019 at about 4:30 AM at Ganj Muradabad, Agra Lucknow Expressway within jurisdiction of PS Bhangarmau, Unnao UP.

sentences.text: Succinctly, the case put forward vide petition is that on 18.05.2019, deceased along with his parents and many other people were travelling from Gurugram to Madhubani, Bihar in a Bus bearing registration No. UP83BT4106 driven by respondent no.1.

Respondent no.1 was driving it at very high speed and was not following traffic rules &
regulations.

The respondent no.1 while driving the bus in aforesaid manner, hit one tractor trolley loaded with watermelons from behind at about 4:30 AM when it was travelling in area of Ganj Muradabad on Agra Lucknow Expressway at Bhangarmau, District Unnao, UP.
The respondent no.1 was not able to control it after same and it turned turtle at the spot of incident resulting in severe injuries to the passengers travelling in it including the deceased.
After the incident, all injured were shifted to Government Hospital, Unnao.
Deceased expired during the treatment.
The incident happened solely due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.01.
Deceased was aged about 07 years and was studying at the time of incident.

The respondent no.1 made all efforts to avoid the incident.

FINAL ARGUMENTS/SUBMISSIONS/CONTENTIONS 9.1
Submissions/contentions of the petitioner side are that the petitioner side has positively proved that the incident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no.01.
Deceased was studying at the time of incident.
He was aged about 07 years at the time of incident.

9.2 Submissions/contentions of the respondent no.01 and 02 are that the incident happened solely due to negligence of driver of the tractor trolley.

sentences.text: In civil matters the facts are required to be established by way of preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubt as is required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is not as heavy as it is in a criminal case and in a claim petition under The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, this burden is even lesser than a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the prepositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of "Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors."

This Tribunal has also given thoughtful consideration to arguments addressed by Ld. Counsels for the parties.
10.3 This petition is one of the 13 connected petitions of the incident in question.
The 5 major injured petitioners have deposed that on the day of incident the respondent no.1 was driving the bus in question at very high speed ignoring traffic rules and regulations.
He was also not caring about other people Ram Vinod Yadav & Anr. vs. Bijoy Mondal & Ors.

He hit the bus in a tractor trolley loaded with watermelons from behind.
He was not able to control the bus even after the incident and it turned turtle.
The rashness and negligence in driving of the bus in question is writ large from the circumstances of the case as the respondent no.1 hit his bus in the tractor trolley from behind.
It is also evident from the fact that not only he hit the bus in tractor trolley from behind but he was also not able to control it after the incident, due to which, it turned turtle.
The circumstances of the incident leaves no doubt that incident happened due to negligence of respondent no.1 only.
10.4 The respondent no.01/driver was the best witness who could have rebutted the case of rashness and negligence of driving of the offending vehicle put forwarded by petitioner/claimant side.
But respondent no.01/driver has chosen not to come in witness box to disprove the case of the petitioner side on said aspect.
In the given circumstances, adverse inference also needs to be drawn against respondents.
Reliance can be placed upon the decision "Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh" 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310 upon said issue/aspect.

Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in its guiding lamp post judgment qua methodology and considerations for assessing/ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular death cases of minors as it is pleaded that deceased was 07 years of age at the time of incident.
11.2 The Hon'ble High court of Delhi in matter of "Chetan Malhotra vs. Lala Ram" 2016 DHC 3863 has held:-

(ii) For inflation-correction, the financial year of 1997- 1998 shall be treated as the "base year"
and the value of the notional income relevant to the date of cause of action shall be computed in the following manner :-
` 15,000/- x A 331 [wherein the figure of `15,000/- represents the notional income specified in the second schedule requiring inflation-correction; A represents the CII for the financial year in which the cause of action arose (i.e. the accident / death occurred); and the figure of 331 represents the CII for the base year]
(iii).
After arriving at an appropriate figure of the present equivalent value of the notional income (i.e. inflation- corrected amount), it shall be rounded off to a figure in next thousands of rupees.

(iv). The amount of notional income thus calculated shall be reduced to two-third, the deduction to the extent of one- third being towards personal & living expenses of the deceased, the balance taken as the annual loss to estate (hereinafter also referred to as "the multiplicand").

(v). For assessment of the pecuniary damages on account of the death of children upto the age of 10 years, the loss to estate shall be calculated, capitalizing the multiplicand, by applying the multiplier of ten (10).
(vi).
For children of the age-group of more than 10 years upto 15 years, the loss to estate shall be calculated by applying the multiplier of fifteen (15).

(vii). For children of the age-group of more than 15 years but less than 18 years, the loss to estate shall be calculated by applying the multiplier of eighteen (18).
(viii).

After the pecuniary loss to estate has been worked out in the manner indicated above, an amount equivalent to the amount thus computed shall be added to it as the composite non- ecuniary damages taking care of not only the conventional heads but also towards future prospects as awarded in R.K. Malik v. Kiran Pal (2009) 14 SCC 1.
(ix).

sentences.text: DETERMINATION OF AGE & MULTIPLIER 11.3
The petitioner(s), in the claim petition has/have claimed that the deceased was aged about 07 years on the date of accident.
The date of incident is 18.05.2019.
As per Post Mortem report of deceased, the deceased was aged about 8 years at the time of incident.
Hence, deceased was 08 years of age at the time of incident and his age is considered accordingly.
He falls in age bracket upto 10 years, hence, multiplier applicable in this matter as per above judgment would be 10.
COMPUTATION OF AWARD 11.4

In view of the abovesaid judgment,
the notional income of the minor has to be computed as Rs.15,000/- X A (Cost Inflation Index for the financial year in which the accident occurred) /331 (CII for the base year 1997-1998).
11.5 CBDT has notified the CII vide circular bearing No. SO1790(E) on 05.06.2017.
The major change in this notification is the introduction of new base year as financial year 2001-2002 instead of financial year 1981-1982.
CII has been notified as 289 for the financial year 2019-20 and the CII for the base year 2001- 2002 is 100.

Accordingly, the formula which has been stated in the said authority needs to be read as under:-
11.6
Thus, Notional Income of the deceased comes to Rs.43,350/- [Rs.15000/-X 289(CII for the year 2021-2022)/100] 11.7

By virtue of para no. 71 (iv) of the said judgment, the said notional income is to be reduced by 2/3rd after deducting 1/3 towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and the remainder has to be treated as annual loss to the estate.

Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in its guiding lamp post judgment qua methodology and considerations for assessing/ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular death cases of minors as it is pleaded that deceased was 07 years of age at the time of incident.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In civil matters the facts are required to be established by way of preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubt as is required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is not as heavy as it is in a criminal case and in a claim petition under The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, this burden is even lesser than a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the prepositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of "Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors."
reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgments in the case of "Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and Ors." 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and "Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.", 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 etc. 10.2
He was also not caring about other people Ram Vinod Yadav & Anr. vs. Bijoy Mondal & Ors.
The circumstances of the incident leaves no doubt that incident happened due to negligence of respondent no.1 only.
But respondent no.01/driver has chosen not to come in witness box to disprove the case of the petitioner side on said aspect.
In the given circumstances, adverse inference also needs to be drawn against respondents.
In totality of circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the claimant side has been able to bring on record such facts which proves almost at the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the incident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration number UP83BT4106 by its driver/respondent no.01 on the date and time of the incident.

By virtue of para no. 71 (iv) of the said judgment, the said notional income is to be reduced by 2/3rd after deducting 1/3 towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and the remainder has to be treated as annual loss to the estate.
Furthermore, by virtue of para no. 71(viii), of the said judgment, a sum equal to loss of estate i.e.
Rs. 2,89,000/- needs to be added towards non pecuniary damages.
In view of above discussions and awards passed under different heads, this Tribunal hereby pass an award of sum of Rs.5,78,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Seventy Eight Thousand Only) in favour of petitioner no.01 and 02 and against the respondents.
In case of any delay, it shall be liable to pay interest at the rate of 9% per annum for the period of delay.
The same has been made effective from 01.01.2019.
